status: owner goal clarified; bounded first slice authorized; broad vocabulary selection not qualified

goals.1a: Language-agnostic known-problem recognition/retrieval returns a value containing one or more separately qualified implementations in any language; the consuming program selects the implementation. Language is not part of recognizer identity.
goals.1b: One informal natural-language description to language-agnostic matched solution value or abstention, with zero clarification questions. The value may contain multiple separately qualified language implementations; the consumer chooses.
goals.2a: Known problem to autonomously composed complete JavaScript/Python program using at most 256 language-specific reusable parameterized macro entries. A whole solution may occupy one entry and form a valid one-macro program. Unbounded stored-answer lookup remains a separate baseline.
goals.2b: Nearby semantic variant to appropriately adapted composition, tested against independently sealed changed requirements and answers.
goals.human: The same semantic macros are available through binary input, counting bindings, constants, control/escape tokens, navigation and corrections as well as macro selections.

intermediate_representation: Optional implementation choice. Keep typed graphs only where they improve validation, composition or measurement; graph architecture is not the objective.
languages: JavaScript and Python are the current corpus/expansion targets, not a restriction on recognition identity. Qualify each implementation separately. Language-specific 2a/2b macro vocabularies/compositions may differ; shared algorithmic structure may guide them without a mandatory shared IR.

existing_precursors.known_catalog: 2501 independently qualified Python answers; no equivalently qualified JavaScript catalog yet.
existing_precursors.teacher_graphs: 24 qualified authored development graphs across 18 problems; preserve original corpus/checkpoint and experiment identities.
existing_precursors.editor_alphabets: Existing ASCII7 and JavaScript/Python byte256 lexical shortcuts are separate unchanged baselines, not the target semantic macro vocabulary.
existing_precursors.model_labels: 43 typed predictor labels are not the target 256-entry language codebook.
existing_precursors.fragment_prototype: 300 candidate closed fragments extracted from 15 fit graphs; paused before sealed comparison/independent scoring; no fragment promotion.

first_slice.candidate_codebooks: Separate versioned JavaScript/Python profiles with 256 addressable positions; initially 12 specified entries, including scope closure, and 244 reserved/unusable entries. Not a complete or selected vocabulary.
first_slice.representation: Explicit macro sequence plus typed binding/literal operands; deterministic source expansion; no arbitrary source hole or query-time autoregressive source generation.
first_slice.tests: Preserve the existing 102 hash-bound independent development tests; score both languages and macro expansions separately after freezing source/streams. Add explicit software tests for scope, malformed streams and numeric boundaries; do not call them fresh semantic generalization.

source_semantics.normalization: One named entry, positional normalized parameter p0, deterministic local slot names, fixed formatting, preserved algorithm/control flow. Store original source plus normalized/expanded source and provenance hashes.
source_semantics.integers: First shared profile uses integer values exactly representable in JavaScript Number, within plus/minus (2^53-1); reject non-integers, booleans-as-integers and overflow. Python's larger integer domain does not silently qualify JavaScript.
source_semantics.lists: Bounded integer lists; append creates a new list in both languages. No accidental input mutation; test input preservation.
source_semantics.maps: Integer-keyed maps; absent lookup takes explicit default. Map mutation is explicit and handles cannot be passed as value operands or returned.
source_semantics.scope: Declarations cannot shadow live bindings; loop/branch locals cannot escape; assignment requires a matching mutable slot; maps are local to one call.
source_semantics.equality: Integer strict equality, not JavaScript coercion.
source_semantics.out_of_scope: General strings, floating point, BigInt, recursion, object identity, exceptions-as-control-flow, async behavior and broad LeetCode interfaces are not qualified by this slice.

token_accounting.macro_ids: Each macro/control selection is one 8-bit ID; unused IDs fail closed.
token_accounting.operands: Count every slot ID, reference/literal tag, signed varint byte, explicit block close and return. No free parameter or constant channel.
token_accounting.framing: Count profile/version/language/signature framing separately and in complete stream total. Preserve bytes for deterministic replay and encode-decode-encode identity.
token_accounting.comparison: Report semantic stream cost against exact ASCII7, UTF-8/byte8 and existing lexical-codebook input costs for the same qualified normalized source. Selection count alone is not total input cost.

next_vocabulary_work: Expand a bounded independently tested JavaScript/Python corpus with pinned provenance and domain/complexity contracts; preserve failures and translation differences.
Mine language-specific normalized AST fragments with explicit free/bound variables, constants, control-flow and effect contracts; parameterize bodies, not names alone.
Select at most256 entries under complete corpus coverage and total input-cost objectives, charging vocabulary description size and escape fallback costs.

Freeze codebook/version and deterministic replay; compare unbounded stored-answer lookup, bounded macro search and autonomous macro prediction separately. Report whole-solution entries and multi-macro compositions separately; both can satisfy the representation.
Use permitted fit families for vocabulary selection. Preserve existing protected66/60 reservation unchanged, and independently seal any new family holdout before mining its solutions.
measurement_axes: representational coverage with independently correct expansions
macro_granularity: Whole solutions are permitted as entries within the fixed256 budget. Report one-macro and multi-macro programs, body size, parameter/binding/constant/escape costs and provenance separately. No hidden unbounded answer table or assertion that fine-grained composition is inherently preferable.
